summary: This specification updates OLSRv2 with an optimization that improves how routing multipoint relays are selected. The optimization retains full interoperability between implementations with and without it.

eli5.summary: Some helpers pass along messages for the group. This picks the helpers better, and old and new versions still work together.

questions: what is the olsrv2 mpr optimization
does olsrv2 mpr optimization break interoperability
subtitle: An optional trim of OLSRv2's routing relay set that can shrink messages without breaking interoperability.

tldr.problem: OLSRv2 selects routing multipoint relays (MPRs) in a way the rationale document found overly prescriptive, so some selected MPRs are unnecessary when link metrics are used.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lets a router remove certain MPRs from the set built under RFC 7181, when a sequence of neighbors can be reached over a shorter total metric distance.
tldr.outcome: The optimization is permissive, can give smaller and fewer messages and never the opposite, and routers with and without it interoperate. It updates RFC 7181.

today: RFC 7187 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 7181. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Context and Motivation
sections.content:
The Optimized Link State Routing Protocol version 2 (OLSRv2, RFC 7181) is a proactive link state routing protocol for mobile ad hoc networks. Compared to its predecessor, RFC 3626, it uses link metrics rather than only minimum-hop routing.

The rationale for link metrics in RFC 7185 describes removing some unnecessarily selected routing multipoint relays (MPRs), but that step was not included in RFC 7181. This specification adds it.
sections.eli5: A network of moving gadgets uses helper gadgets to pass messages along. Some helpers turn out to be unnecessary, and this update lets a router skip them.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.content:
The optimization is simply permissive: there is no requirement for any implementation to include it. Including it is advised because it can, in some cases, create smaller and fewer messages, without ever having the opposite effect.

RFC 7181 requires the routing MPRs to be symmetric 1-hop neighbors that cover all symmetric 2-hop neighbors, while retaining a minimum distance route to each. RFC 7185 indicates this is overly prescriptive. A router using the optimization is still considered compliant, and it interoperates with routers that do not use it.
sections.eli5: You may use the shortcut or not. If you do, you never make things worse, and you can still work with those who do not.

sections.title: Routing MPR Selection
sections.content:
A set of routing MPRs built as specified in RFC 7181 MAY be optimized. Consider a sequence x_0 through x_n of 1-hop neighbors where x_0 is a routing MPR and x_1 through x_n have corresponding 2-hop neighbors y_1 through y_n. If, for each m, the metric distance via x_0 and the preceding 2-hop links is less than the direct distance d1(x_m), then x_1 to x_n may be removed from the routing MPR set if they were selected.

"Corresponding elements" means elements that represent the same router. All the needed information is available from the neighborhood discovery protocol, NHDP (RFC 6130).
sections.eli5: If a message can reach a neighbor faster by going through a helper you already have, the extra helper is not needed and can be dropped.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The update adds no new protocol signals and does not change how received signals are processed. It may remove unneeded routers from the routing MPR sets, which also removes the need to include that information in Topology Control (TC) messages. Because the information is not used when included, no additional security considerations arise beyond those in RFC 7181.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is sent and nothing is treated differently, so nothing new can go wrong.
